_comment: The Kali tool groups, as anonymOS ships them. Kali Linux is Debian plus a curated set of
security tools organised into kali-tools-* metapackages; this is the same idea for anonymOS.
anonymOS runs musl (its Linux personality is Alpine's libc), so a tool runs here when it is
packaged for Alpine -- it is the SAME upstream program (nmap is nmap). Each group below lists
the tools we want in it; scripts/pack-software-catalog.py keeps only the ones that actually
exist in the Alpine main/community index it harvested, and emits one virtual metapackage per
group whose dependencies are exactly those survivors. Installing the metapackage installs each
of them through the ordinary pinned-and-verified apk path, into the domain that asked -- the
Kali domain. The metapackage itself ships no bytes; every file is a real, checksummed Alpine
apk. A tool on a list that Alpine does not package is simply left out of that image's group,
and the catalog's Security category still lists it as browsable-not-installable like any other.
These are tools for authorised security work -- penetration testing engagements you are
permitted to run, CTF, lab practice, research, and defence. The domain is isolated and routed
like any other; what it may reach is the domain's network policy, set in the Domain Manager.
